house.description: Cost-sharing for certain office visits for infants, children, and adolescents prohibited.

House.text: Introduction and first reading, referred to Health Finance and Policy

bill_text.text_with_changes:
A bill for an act relating to health insurance; prohibiting cost-sharing for certain office visits for infants, children, and adolescents; amending Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 62Q.46, by adding a subdivision.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 62Q.46, is amended by adding a subdivision to read:

[+Subd. 2a.+]

[+Infants, children, and adolescents.+]

[+(a) Notwithstanding subdivision 2, a health plan company is prohibited from imposing cost-sharing requirements with respect to an office visit if: +]

[+(1) the primary purpose of the visit is to provide infants, children, and adolescents with evidence-informed preventive care and screenings identified in comprehensive guidelines supported by the Health Resources and Services Administration; and +]

[+(2) the office visit is 15 minutes or less in duration. +]

[+(b) If an office visit meets the requirements of paragraph (a), a health plan company must not prohibit a health care provider from billing for preventive items or services that are billed separately or tracked separately as individual encounter data. +]
bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to health insurance; prohibiting cost-sharing for certain office visits for infants, children, and adolescents; amending Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 62Q.46, by adding a subdivision.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.
Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 62Q.46, is amended by adding a subdivision to read:

Subd. 2a.

Infants, children, and adolescents.

(a) Notwithstanding subdivision 2, a health plan company is prohibited from imposing cost-sharing requirements with respect to an office visit if:

(1) the primary purpose of the visit is to provide infants, children, and adolescents with evidence-informed preventive care and screenings identified in comprehensive guidelines supported by the Health Resources and Services Administration; and

(2) the office visit is 15 minutes or less in duration.

(b) If an office visit meets the requirements of paragraph (a), a health plan company must not prohibit a health care provider from billing for preventive items or services that are billed separately or tracked separately as individual encounter data.
additions: (a) Notwithstanding subdivision 2, a health plan company is prohibited from imposing cost-sharing requirements with respect to an office visit if:

(1) the primary purpose of the visit is to provide infants, children, and adolescents with evidence-informed preventive care and screenings identified in comprehensive guidelines supported by the Health Resources and Services Administration; and
(2) the office visit is 15 minutes or less in duration.

(b) If an office visit meets the requirements of paragraph (a), a health plan company must not prohibit a health care provider from billing for preventive items or services that are billed separately or tracked separately as individual encounter data.
